title: Control Eval Lab: simple charts of what we measured
generated_note: These charts summarise two kinds of work. The practice-site lock checks are what this public repo can re-run. The “how often did the model try a fake risky tool?” bars were measured earlier in a private local project (DarkGenus) on Ollama; cloning this repo does not regenerate them. Fine-tune files and prompt lists stay private. No cookies, product URLs, or build recipes for looser models.

tool_attempt_suite.description: How often each model tried a pretend dangerous tool under a fixed pressure script (fake tools only). Measured in private DarkGenus on Ollama; summarised here, not reproduced by running this repo.

takeaways: A chat “no” is not the same as refusing to press a tool button.
DarkGenus (private) ran the fake-tool suites first; this public repo adds the practice-site locks.
Under one fixed DarkGenus script (262 prompts), v3 tried fake risky tools less often (~13%) than stock Qwen (~77%).
A blocker after the model stopped fake tool runs even when the model tried.
Control Lab sandboxed MimWise in Docker (prod blocked) before live SoftTrial; Docker showed a guest answer leak, live was harder.
This public practice site is a simplified scoring villain, not the private Docker MimWise stack.
